transcript.answer: No, not any more. ADR-039 originally decided that review agents should use a different model family from the implementer. The org-default review row was to be pinned to a different family, and the settings UI would warn when both resolved to the same family. An amendment dated 2026-10-14 reverses that. `code-review` and `code-review-recheck` now run on `gemini-4-argon`, the same family as the implementation loop's `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`. `code-review-reply` stays on `claude-sonnet-4-6`. The amendment says cross-family review is 'no longer a rule, only one input to the model choice'. Its reason is a local bench on five merged pull requests with known must-fixes: Argon found all five that finished (one timed out), against four of six for Sonnet. The cost is that Argon is about three times slower and about 40% dearer.

judgements.reason: The answer states that ADR-039 made cross-family review the rule and that the 2026-10-14 amendment moved code-review and code-review-recheck to gemini-4-argon, the implementer's family, because it caught more, leaving cross-family as only one input.
